instruction.text:
Amy has planted a special kind of grass in her garden that grows by exactly four inches each month.

Fill in the gaps in the table to find out how tall Amy’s lawn is at the end of each month.

trainers.layout:
a1 b1 c1 d1 e1 f1
a2 b2 c2 d2 e2 f2

instruction.text:
For every glass of chocolate milk, Ellie uses three teaspoons of cocoa powder.

Fill in the gaps in the table to find out how many teaspoons of cocoa powder she needs for each number of glasses of chocolate milk.

trainers.layout:
a1 b1 c1 d1 e1 f1
a2 b2 c2 d2 e2 f2

instruction.text:
Hilal had £50 in her piggy bank in January. Every month after that her parents give her £5.

Fill in the gaps in the table to find out how many pounds Hilal has in her piggy bank each month.

trainers.layout:
a1 a2
b1 b2
c1 c2
d1 d2
e1 e2 
f1 f2

instruction.text:
Frank is renting a film. There is a one time fee of £2 for renting the film, and for each day after the first day, it costs £1 to rent the film.

Fill in the gaps in the table to find out how many pounds Frank has to pay depending on how many days he keeps the film.

trainers.layout:
a1 a2
b1 b2
c1 c2
d1 d2
e1 e2 
f1 f2
